links.outcome: Reproducibility of fracture detection across five repeated runs per model (Fleiss' kappa)
links.effect: GPT-5 Pro κ = 0.71; Gemini 2.5 Pro κ = 0.57; Claude Sonnet 4.5 κ = 0.33 (instability); Mistral κ = 0.88 despite 38.5% accuracy (systematic error).
links.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.5 showed low accuracy (33.8%) and consistency (κ = 0.33), reflecting instability.

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of MLLMs for hand fracture detection on plain radiographs
links.effect: Accuracy ranged from 33.8% to 64.3% (GPT-5 Pro highest at 64.3%); scaphoid fractures remained challenging; models not reliable standalone tools.
links.quote: At present, MLLMs should be regarded as experimental diagnostic reasoning systems rather than reliable standalone tools for clinical fracture detection.

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and repeated-inference stability/consistency of four multimodal large language models on hand fracture radiographs without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
